newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Arakis boosted by buyback.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Arakis boosted by buyback.

text.p: News of a share buyback program and the departure of three senior executives sparked demand for Arakis Energy Corp's American Depositary Receipts on Friday, with the issue jumping to the top of the Nasdaq's most-active list.
By noon, Arakis was up 3/8, or 12.75 percent, at 3-5/16. With about half of the session complete, volume was more than 6.2 million shares, twice the average daily volume.
"The stock was for sale this morning. It must have been the rumor mill, but then it rallied back. I think the buyback is the biggest factor," a market maker in Arakis ADRs said.
Earlier Friday, Arakis said it would respond to a recent call from a large number of its stockholders by approving a share buyback plan.
The company said the program would give management discretion to make purchases of up to a total of 10 percent of Arakis's stock.
The company said it had about US$50 million in deposit and no immediate need for the cash.
"In the opinion of the board of directors, the common shares are an attractive investment for the company," it said.

Also, Arakis confirmed the departure of three vice presidents: Peter Holstein, David Robinson and David Harrison, all of whom played significant roles in events leading up to Arakis's recent announcement of a US$1.0 billion deal to develop its oil concessions in Sudan.
